# Release watcher: operations guide

Version 1.0.0 of the specification: 1 monitor, 2 jobs, 0 dependencies and 0 endpoints. For the people who run the live system: where it runs, what to look at each day, what to do when a monitor's objective is missed, what runs on its own, what it depends on, and how its data is saved and brought back.

## 1. Where it runs

| Environment | Purpose | Run by | Promotes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| production | The host whose services the watcher keeps current. | vendor |   |

## 2. Daily checklist

What to look at on the live system each day. Tick the last column as each is seen to be as expected.

| Check | What to look at | Expected | Seen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monitor watcher-running (production) | Whether the release watcher's unit is active. | The unit is active at every check, each minute of the day. |   |
| Job sweep | Its last run, every PT1M. | It ran, and failed on no item. |   |
| Job prune | Its last run, on the schedule `0 3 * * *` (UTC). | It ran, and failed on no item. |   |
| Process releaseWatcher | That it is running. | It is running and healthy: it has asked the registry within the last two minutes, and tells the service manager so. |   |
| Process releasePrune | Its last run. | It ran, and exited 0. |   |

## 3. Monitors

### watcher-running

Whether the release watcher's unit is active. In production. Objective: The unit is active at every check, each minute of the day.

Verifies RW-2.

When the objective is missed:

| Step | Action | Check |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Read why it stopped | Read the unit's journal from the last start. | The error of its last run is known. |
| 2. Start it again | Fix what the error names and start the unit. | The unit is active and the monitor clears. |

## 4. Jobs

What the system runs on its own. A job acts as its role and may do only what the role's permissions allow.

| Job | Starts | Acts as | After a failure | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sweep | every PT1M | installer | not tried again | Asks the registry for the latest release of each service and installs one newer than the installed. |
| prune | on the schedule `0 3 * * *` (UTC) | installer | not tried again | Removes the releases of each service older than its last three. |

## 5. Processes

The programs the service manager starts and watches. A process acts as no role: the jobs it runs act as theirs.

| Process | Runs | Jobs | Restarted | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| releaseWatcher | always, from the host's start | sweep | when it fails, after PT5S; given up after 5 starts within PT10M | Asks the registry for a new release of each service and installs it. |
| releasePrune | when a job it runs is due | prune | never | Removes old releases each night. |

**Origin on releaseWatcher:** stated in The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-watcher.service.

**Note on releaseWatcher:** From The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-watcher.service: Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5s, StartLimitBurst=5 within StartLimitIntervalSec=10min, RestartPreventExitStatus=78, TimeoutStopSec=30s, WatchdogSec=2min, ExecReload sends SIGHUP. <../sources/units>

**Origin on releasePrune:** stated in The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-prune.timer.

**Note on releasePrune:** From The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-prune.timer: OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00:00 on a host whose clock is UTC, which the job prune's schedule says. <../sources/units>

### releaseWatcher

Reads the settings registryAddress, registryToken, logLevel when it starts; the section Settings says what each is.

| Signal | What it does |
|---|---|
| SIGTERM | finishes the release it is installing, then exits 0, within PT30S |
| SIGHUP | reads its settings again |

| Exit status | Meaning | Started again |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | it was asked to stop | as Restarted says |
| 78 | a setting is missing or wrong | never |

Healthy when it has asked the registry within the last two minutes, and tells the service manager so. Looked at every PT2M.

Watched by the monitor watcher-running; the section Monitors says what to do when one is missed.

### releasePrune

The specification does not say which signals it honours; each is written under the process's signals.

| Exit status | Meaning | Started again |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | it removed what was older than the last three releases | as Restarted says |
| 1 | a release could not be removed | as Restarted says |

## 9. Settings

Every setting the system reads at run time. A secret's value is never written here; its description says where the value comes from.

| Setting | Type | Secret | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| registryAddress | string |  | The address of the registry the watcher asks for new releases. |
| registryToken | string | yes | The token the watcher reads the registry with, from the environment file only root reads. |
| logLevel | string |  | How much the watcher logs. |
